Frequency once per day

Effect You can call on the elements with ease. You become quickened until the end of your rage. You can use your extra action to use actions or activities with the impulse trait.

Grip Needle.name: Grip Needle
Grip Needle.description: This immensely tiny blade requires intense strength to wield properly instead of the normal dextrous requirements of a knife due to its miniscule size.

Call the Breach.name: Call the Breach
Call the Breach.description:
You draw forth the energies of the portal to the breach themselves and manifest its nature. You create difficult terrain in a @Template[distance:30|type:emanation] that lasts 1 minute and produces an effect depending on your selected plane. This ability gains the traits associated with your plane.

Plane

Effect

Astral

The intensity of dreams and fire flourish within your emanation. Figments of creatures appear within the area, providing flanking for you and your allies as if they were creatures that could make attacks against your enemies.

Ethereal

The ephemeral natures of the ethereal take root. Creatures within the emanation gain a fly speed of 10 feet, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1}, and resistance to physical damage equal to your level unless the damage would be dealt by a weapon or unarmed attack with the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.JQdwHECogcTzdd8R]{Ghost Touch} property. @UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-barbarians.misc.DowZBFFAGGpiXTC7]{Effect: Call the Ethereal Breach}

Netherworld

The swirling shadows arise from the beyond. The area becomes dim light or darkness if it would already be dim light. You immediately extinguish any non-magical light sources and attempt to counteract magical light sources. Your counteract rank for this attempt is equal to half your level rounded up, and you use your class DC - 10 for the counteract check. The flat check to target you while @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed} in this darkness is 7 instead of 5.

First World

The shifting plane of the eldest is truly unruly, and you can call forth its tumultuous nature. You can spend a single action with the concentrate and rage traits to create a @Template[type:burst|distance:10] of greater difficult terrain within the area that lasts the duration.

Road Rage.name: Road Rage
Road Rage.description: You are at your angriest when behind the wheels of a vehicle. You gain the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.feats-srd.Item.BocFD2KV0qgUC76x]{Additional Lore} skill feat for Driving Lore, and the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.uS3qDAgOkZ7b8ERL]{Drive} action gains the Rage trait for you while you are raging. Whenever you pilot a vehicle while raging, you add your Rage damage to your vehicle's collision damage. If an activity would call you to Stride, such as Sudden Charge, you can instead use Drive for a number of actions that you would have used Stride applying any restrictions or reductions in speed to your vehicle's movement.

Raging.name: Raging
Raging.description: Your rage is exemplified in violent and uncontrollable anger. This makes no changes to your existing features.

Instinct Crown (Disaster).name: Instinct Crown (Disaster)
Instinct Crown (Disaster).description:
An instinct crown is a magical headpiece imbued with the essence of instincts that barbarians draw upon in combat. Each crown is fashioned to represent the instinct it's tied to, such as a wolf's head for an animal instinct crown or a simple helmet with Jotun runes for a giant instinct crown. When worn, the crown allows you to tap further into your instincts, granting you even greater benefits if the crown's essence matches your instinct. You must be able to Rage to use the crown's activations.

Activate F envision

Frequency once per day

Trigger You roll initiative

Effect You Rage, gaining 10 additional temporary Hit Points.

Activate 2 command, envision

Requirements The crown's instinct matches your barbarian instinct

Frequency once per day

Effect You bring disaster and ruin as the herald of the end. Creatures that end their turn within the area of your emanation take persistent damage of the same amount and type as the emanation would deal.

Revitalizing Blood.name: Revitalizing Blood
Revitalizing Blood.description:
You bleed yourself to revitalize others. You take @Damage[(floor(@actor.level/2))[persistent,bleed]] damage equal to half your level and choose one ally within 30 feet. Each time you take this persistent bleed damage, you grant your ally temporary Hit Points equal to the same amount that last until the beginning of your next turn.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-barbarians.misc.saANGEZnZQX0FTn4]{Effect: Revitalizing Blood}

Heedless Swig.name: Heedless Swig
Heedless Swig.description: You pull a flask, tankard or vial down in the middle of combat, down it, and throw it to the wayside, reinvigorated. You Interact to draw a drink or liquid and then Interact again to consume a drink or liquid you are holding, gaining its effects as normal for consuming the liquid. If the liquid was an ingested poison, you may choose to get an automatic failure on your saving throw to gain a +1 status bonus to damage for 2 rounds plus a number of rounds equal to half the level of the item. Consuming poisons in this way causes the effects to lose their onset period and affect you immediately. The status bonus to damage increases to +2 if you are 7th level, or +4 if you are 15th level.

Lashing Branches.name: Lashing Branches
Lashing Branches.description: Your hands transform into twisting wooden tendrils when you rage, allowing you to strike at your enemies from afar. You gain a lashing branch unarmed strike, which deals 1d6 slashing damage and has the reach and versatile B traits. If you have critical specialization, your unarmed attack also gains the shove trait.

World-Shaking Throw.name: World-Shaking Throw
World-Shaking Throw.description:
The force at which you throw things is truly titanic. While raging, you double the range of your thrown weapons. On a critical hit with a thrown weapon, the target must attempt a @Check[type:reflex|dc:resolve(@actor.attributes.classDC.value)] save against your class DC or be knocked @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}.

You can attempt to lift heavy objects using your Athletics, such as logs or boulders, with a single Interact action. When you successfully lift a heavy object, it becomes an improvised weapon with the thrown trait and a range of 20 feet. Regardless of the result of a Strike made with a heavy object, the object moves to the location it was thrown and remains there as an obstacle, moving any creatures that would occupy its new space to the nearest adjacent square. The damage die for a heavy object is d12 and deals an additional damage die for each size above Medium.

DO YOU EVEN LIFT?

Any object greater than 10 Bulk is considered a heavy object and the size of the object generally determines its default bulk value with a Large object being 12 Bulk, a Huge object being 24 Bulk, Gargantuan object being 48 Bulk. Objects that have different densities, such as solid stone or a hollow tree, may increase or decrease this Bulk value (subject to GM discretion), but the Athletics DC to lift a heavy object is equal to 20 plus the Bulk value above your Bulk limit (10 plus your Strength modifier) and you must attempt a new Athletics check each turn you continue to hold the object.

Frenzied Mixer.name: Frenzied Mixer
Frenzied Mixer.description:
Cost 1 versatile vial

You have learned to use your mixtures without an apparatus. You create a single alchemical mutagen of your level or lower that’s in your formula book without having to spend the normal monetary cost in alchemical raw materials or needing to attempt a Crafting check and then Interact to throw the mutagen to an ally within 20 feet. This item has the infused trait.

Call of the Ancestor.name: Call of the Ancestor
Call of the Ancestor.description:
Requirements You’re wielding your vestige.

You listen for the call of the ancestor in your vestige weapon. You concentrate on your vestige weapon, and attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seek} for its voice by attempting a @Check[type:perception|dc:@self.level] check against a standard DC of your level. If your check is a success, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your next attack roll with your vestige weapon this turn, or a +2 circumstance bonus if your check was a critical success.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-barbarians.misc.NQvBAbJB8uUlmntt]{Effect: Call of the Ancestor}

Hulk-Pull Shot.name: Hulk-Pull Shot
Hulk-Pull Shot.description:
2 or 3

Requirements You’re wielding a weapon in the bow group.

You pull your bowstring back with unprecedented strength. Make a ranged Strike with the required weapon. The Strike gains the following effects in addition to the normal effects of a Strike.

Critical Success You deal your additional damage from Rage on your Strike and the target is knocked back 10 feet. If you used the 3-action version of this activity, if the target contacts a barrier or object, it is knocked @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{prone} after it contacts the barrier or object. This is forced movement.

Success As critical success, but you only deal half your Rage damage and the target is knocked back 5 feet.

Critical Failure Your bow gains the broken condition until you spend 10 minutes restringing it with the Repair action.

Harness Bloodline.name: Harness Bloodline
Harness Bloodline.description: You gain your bloodline’s initial bloodline spell. If you don’t already have one, you also gain a focus pool of 1 Focus Point, which you can Refocus without any special effort.

Instinct Crown (Alchemical).name: Instinct Crown (Alchemical)
Instinct Crown (Alchemical).description:
An instinct crown is a magical headpiece imbued with the essence of instincts that barbarians draw upon in combat. Each crown is fashioned to represent the instinct it's tied to, such as a wolf's head for an animal instinct crown or a simple helmet with Jotun runes for a giant instinct crown. When worn, the crown allows you to tap further into your instincts, granting you even greater benefits if the crown's essence matches your instinct. You must be able to Rage to use the crown's activations.

Activate F envision

Frequency once per day

Trigger You roll initiative

Effect You Rage, gaining 10 additional temporary Hit Points.

Activate 2 command, envision

Requirements The crown's instinct matches your barbarian instinct

Frequency once per day

Effect Your body becomes resistant to the drawbacks of alchemy. You can ignore one mutagenic drawback as long as you are raging and you deal 2 additional damage with attacks you gained from a mutagen.

Destined Kill.name: Destined Kill
Destined Kill.description:
Sometimes, a warrior is sworn to defeat a solitary and spectacular foe in single combat. Choose an enemy creature within 30 feet to become your destined kill. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to attack rolls against the chosen enemy and become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AdPVz7rbaVSRxHFg]{fascinated} by them. You take a –1 circumstance penalty to attack rolls against creatures other than the target. You immediately end your stance if you take hostile actions against creatures other than the target of your destined kill, unless they would be required to engage with your target, such as attempting to Escape from the grabbed condition (subject to GM discretion).

If you reduce your destined kill to 0 Hit Points your stance immediately ends and you gain temporary Hit Points equal to your level that last for as long as you are raging. If the creature was above your level, you also gain a +2 status bonus to Will saves until your rage ends.

Walk With Spirits.name: Walk With Spirits
Walk With Spirits.description: You become a raging spirit. You become incorporeal and gain a fly Speed equal to half your Speed. Strikes against corporeal creatures when you choose to change your damage to spirit damage affect corporeal creatures as normal and your raging resistance changes to be resistance to all damage (except force). These effects last until your rage ends.

Despairing.name: Despairing
Despairing.description:
Your fervor is not fueled by anger, but by despair. Perhaps you feel terrible sadness for your past actions, your present situation, or even the fact that you must commit such violence! You do not gain the Quick Tempered free action. After you take damage while raging, as long as you did not gain the dying or unconscious conditions from the damage, you become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-barbarians.misc.Item.xVAGPe1NX6QEwQ7O]{invigorated} until the end of your next turn. You gain the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-barbarians.misc.Item.fblNfvSAeKRoJHVD]{Welcome Misery} action.

Invigoration Bonus You gain temporary Hit Points and a +1 status bonus to saves against auditory effects.

Absorb Power.name: Absorb Power
Absorb Power.description:
Trigger You take damage from a spell.

You absorb the power of enemy spells, leveraging them to empower your attacks. Your melee Strikes deal your additional rage damage until the end of your next turn and the damage type changes to be the same as the damage of the triggering spell. If the spell deals more than one type of damage, you choose which damage type your Strikes gain when the spell’s damage is resolved.

Blood Surge.name: Blood Surge
Blood Surge.description:
flourish

You surge forth with a burst of energy, exuded from your own blood. You explode with energy that deals 1d4 force damage to creatures in the area and you must include yourself in the area, but you treat your degree of success on your save as one step better. You deal your additional damage from your blood rage as normal for casting a spell. If your melee Strikes are currently empowered by your blood rage, you can choose to change the damage type of this spell to be the same damage type as the additional damage on your Strikes.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d4.

We Ride!.name: We Ride!
We Ride!.description:
Requirements Your animal companion has the mount special ability and is raging.

You were born to rage and ride with your companion and do so fluidly. You @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.q9nbyIF0PEBqMtYe]{Command} your animal companion to Stride toward you and take its support action. If your animal companion’s Stride moves through a square within your reach, you may spend your reaction to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.PM5jvValFkbFH3TV]{Mount} your animal companion as it enters the square during its movement.

Explosive Blood.name: Explosive Blood
Explosive Blood.description: You channel up mighty power in your hand, and release it in a cataclysmic blast. If your next action is to Cast a Spell that would deal the additional damage from Rage and would also damage you, you double the additional damage from Rage until the end of your next turn. This increase in damage applies to your melee Strikes and spells you cast, including the spell you modified with this action.

Instinct Crown (Zealot).name: Instinct Crown (Zealot)
Instinct Crown (Zealot).description:
An instinct crown is a magical headpiece imbued with the essence of instincts that barbarians draw upon in combat. Each crown is fashioned to represent the instinct it's tied to, such as a wolf's head for an animal instinct crown or a simple helmet with Jotun runes for a giant instinct crown. When worn, the crown allows you to tap further into your instincts, granting you even greater benefits if the crown's essence matches your instinct. You must be able to Rage to use the crown's activations.

Activate F envision

Frequency once per day

Trigger You roll initiative

Effect You Rage, gaining 10 additional temporary Hit Points.

Activate 2 command, envision

Requirements The crown's instinct matches your barbarian instinct

Frequency once per day

Effect You call upon your god to answer your call in a shouted prayer. You treat all enemies during this rage as if they were enemies of your deity. Once during your Rage, when you make an attack roll against a creature that would normally qualify as an enemy of your deity you can roll twice and take the better result. This is a fortune effect.

Raging Support.name: Raging Support
Raging Support.description:
Requirements Your animal companion is raging.

Your animal companion’s support is fueled by rage. When your animal companion takes the support action, the additional damage from your rage is increased by 1. If you are at least 7th level, instead increase the additional damage from your rage by 2, or by 4 if you have greater weapon specialization.

Language of the Beasts.name: Language of the Beasts
Language of the Beasts.description: Violence is the language all creatures speak, and you are fluent in it. You can communicate with living creatures that do not speak a language through body language, grunts, roars, or other methods. Though you cannot communicate exact words or details, you can learn rudimentary information from them and even make Deception, Diplomacy, or Intimidation checks against them as if you shared a language but only simple emotions can be conveyed. Though it might not stop them from taking hostile actions if they already intended to, non-hostile creatures will generally give you time to make your case.

Obstinate.name: Obstinate
Obstinate.description:
Your movements are rigid and slow, your resolve firm and ferocious. You do not gain the Quick Tempered free action. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saves and DCs against forced movement or effects that would give you the prone condition while raging. If you did not move more than 30 feet during your turn while raging, you become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-barbarians.misc.Item.xVAGPe1NX6QEwQ7O]{invigorated} until the end of your next turn. You gain the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-barbarians.misc.Item.pi9t13IlpY1UohRc]{Stand Firm} action.

Invigoration Bonus You gain temporary Hit Points and your circumstance bonus to saves and DCs against forced movement and the prone condition increases to +2.

Warped Bloodsurge.name: Warped Bloodsurge
Warped Bloodsurge.description: You've learned to alter the eruptions of magic that you release into different shapes. When you cast @UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-barbarians.items.hiqoZc3SW8BAuTOO]{Blood Surge}, you can change the area into a @Template[distance:15|type:cone] or a @Template[distance:30|type:line] instead of an emanation centered on you. You still take damage from blood surge as if you were in the area.

Carve the World.name: Carve the World
Carve the World.description:
Trigger You would critically succeed at a Strike.

Your attacks are so mighty that by the end of a battle, you might have permanently carved the battlefield with scars that will go down in legend. The birth of a river from the slash of your sword, the creation of a chasm by the swing of a hammer, or a valley being carved through a mountain pass by the hurl of your javelin; your impossible deeds will live long after you in the way you carve the world.

When you would critically hit a creature or an object, you may choose to sunder the battlefield around you. Your Strike gains the death trait and the following effects in addition to the normal effects, based on the kind of damage your weapon deals. You may do other cinematic effects that do not affect the battlefield based on other weapon damage, such as a flaming property rune permanently burning up all the leaves from a forest in an instant, or a shocking property rune turning a beach's sand to glass.

Bludgeoning You create deep craters where your attack lands. The crater appears out to a @Template[distance:30|type:burst] with the target of your Strike as the center, causing all creatures in the area to fall the distance to the edge of the burst and take falling damage as appropriate. You and the target of the triggering Strike do not take this falling damage. Traveling in any direction other than towards the center while in the area is considered difficult terrain.

Piercing You pierce tunnels and walkways through the most impossible of areas. You destroy all obstacles and natural features within a @Template[distance:60|type:line] that includes the target and starts from an edge of your square. This area becomes difficult terrain and creatures occupying the area are automatically moved to the nearest space outside of the area. This is forced movement.

Slashing You carve all standing obstacles in the battlefield. You damage all obstacles taller than your square in a @Template[distance:45|type:cone] and deal slashing damage equal to twice the triggering Strikes weapon damage. This damage ignores any hardness. If this would destroy the object, it instead appears unharmed until the end of your next turn, after which it collapses and creates greater difficult terrain in its area and surrounding squares.

Instinct Crown (Vestige).name: Instinct Crown (Vestige)
Instinct Crown (Vestige).description:
An instinct crown is a magical headpiece imbued with the essence of instincts that barbarians draw upon in combat. Each crown is fashioned to represent the instinct it's tied to, such as a wolf's head for an animal instinct crown or a simple helmet with Jotun runes for a giant instinct crown. When worn, the crown allows you to tap further into your instincts, granting you even greater benefits if the crown's essence matches your instinct. You must be able to Rage to use the crown's activations.

Activate F envision

Frequency once per day

Trigger You roll initiative

Effect You Rage, gaining 10 additional temporary Hit Points.

Activate 2 command, envision

Requirements The crown's instinct matches your barbarian instinct

Frequency once per day

Effect You have the power of your ancestor. You take on the form of your ancestor more fully than before, increasing your physical and mental prowess in the process. You gain a +2 status bonus to saves.

Instinct Crown (Ligneous).name: Instinct Crown (Ligneous)
Instinct Crown (Ligneous).description:
An instinct crown is a magical headpiece imbued with the essence of instincts that barbarians draw upon in combat. Each crown is fashioned to represent the instinct it's tied to, such as a wolf's head for an animal instinct crown or a simple helmet with Jotun runes for a giant instinct crown. When worn, the crown allows you to tap further into your instincts, granting you even greater benefits if the crown's essence matches your instinct. You must be able to Rage to use the crown's activations.

Activate F envision

Frequency once per day

Trigger You roll initiative

Effect You Rage, gaining 10 additional temporary Hit Points.

Activate 2 command, envision

Requirements The crown's instinct matches your barbarian instinct

Frequency once per day

Effect Your skin heals wounds as though it were a fast growing plant. You gain fast healing equal to half your level.

Furious Outburst.name: Furious Outburst
Furious Outburst.description:
Trigger You or an ally fail a Diplomacy check that would change a creature's attitude.

You lose your patience and snap at another creature, bellowing out your communication bluntly and clearly. Attempt a check using @Check[type:intimidation] against the same DC as the triggering check, and you use your result on Intimidation instead of the triggering check for the purposes of determining the outcome. Decrease the DC of the check by 2 if the creature’s attitude is Indifferent or better before the triggering check is resolved.

Lingering Clarity.name: Lingering Clarity
Lingering Clarity.description: Your clarity percolates through your emotional state, allowing you to tap into some of your more difficult tasks. You use @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.feats-srd.Item.vRXPsMbyuvoPvbAQ]{Moment of Clarity} and gain the effects for as long as you remain raging. When you Activate an Item or Cast a Spell, if it has the concentrate trait and lacks the rage trait you immediately end your stance after you complete the action or activity.

Decay Strike.name: Decay Strike
Decay Strike.description:
You channel the decay that ravages your body into a powerful blow. Make a Strike with an attack that would deal additional poison damage from your Rage.

Critical Success The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2}.

Success As critical success, except the creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1}.

Invigorating Speech.name: Invigorating Speech
Invigorating Speech.description:
You stand before your allies and remind them why they fight. You spend 1 minute giving up to 100 creatures an emotionally charging speech that gives them a fraction of your conviction before battle. Make an @Check[type:intimidation] check against a standard DC for the highest level creature targeted by your speech. Regardless of the result, targeted creatures are temporarily immune to your Invigorating Speech for 1 day.

Critical Success Your speech ignites a fervor in them that they did not know was there. The creatures immediately recover 35 Hit Points. If the creature enters an encounter in the next hour related to your speech, it gains 15 temporary Hit Points and a +2 status bonus to saves against death and fear effects that last for 1 minute.

Success Your words stoke a flame in their hearts. As critical success, except the creature recovers 20 Hit Points and gains 10 temporary Hit Points.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-barbarians.misc.XfvfGuGuvwpKIrco]{Effect: Invigorating Speech}

Furious Domain.name: Furious Domain
Furious Domain.description: Your rage and servitude has been recognized by the gods, and you have been rewarded. You gain the advanced domain spell from the same domain you selected for your initial domain spell and it gains the rage trait. You become an expert in spell attack rolls and spell DCs.

Hazardous Rift.name: Hazardous Rift
Hazardous Rift.description: You can invoke the energies associated with your plane to come forth in your illusions. Creatures that end their turn inside the difficult terrain created by your @UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-barbarians.misc.WByBCNNAEk7x2apk]{Breach Blow} take damage equal to your additional damage from Rage with a @Check[basic:true|type:will|against:classDC] save against your class DC. The damage type for your hazardous terrain is your choice of mental or spirit damage.

Alchemical Instinct.name: Alchemical Instinct
Alchemical Instinct.description:
You use strange chemical concoctions to enhance your anger into an unimaginable fury. You might be a meek scientist who uses mutagens as an outlet for your most violent impulses, or you might be an already impressive hulk that takes your powers a step further through alchemical admixtures.

Instinct Ability—Mutagenic Rage Whether through breathing in bizarre fumes or pipes ainjecting reagents directly into your blood, you undergo terrible change when you rage. You gain the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.feats-srd.is3Oz9wt11lNq62K]{Alchemical Crafting} skill feat and a blank @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.qCEOZ6109Yo34tRx]{formula book} for free. You start with a standard formula book, which contains the formulas for two common 1st-rank alchemical mutagens of your choice, in addition to the formulas gained from Alchemical Crafting. Each time you gain a level, you learn the formula for one common alchemical mutagen of any level of item you can create. During your daily preparations, you can create a number of versatile vials equal to 2 plus your Intelligence modifier.

Your @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.a9PzINjFTO5GvAJN]{Quick-Tempered} free action can be triggered by consuming a mutagen during the first round of an encounter in addition to its initial trigger. While under the effects of a mutagen, your additional damage from rage increases from 2 to 3, and you gain additional temporary Hit Points equal to half the item level of the mutagen you consumed in addition to the temporary Hit Points you gained from Rage. You cannot enter a Rage if you consume a mutagen that would give you a penalty to attack rolls and consuming a mutagen that does so immediately ends your Rage.

You gain the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-barbarians.misc.i0Urwze7pbBPVx3X]{Mad Science} action and a special apparatus you affix to your body that aids you in mutagen consumption. Your apparatus weighs 1 Bulk and can be worn. You can spend 1 minute to don your apparatus. You can store up to 3 versatile vials in your apparatus and can store a versatile vial in your apparatus by spending 1 minute isolating the various components of the mixture inside it.

Specialization Ability (7th) When you use mutagenic rage, you increase the additional damage from Rage from 3 to 7 and increase the number of mutagens you can store in your apparatus to 4. If you have greater weapon specialization, instead increase the damage from Mutagenic Rage to 13 and to 7 while not under the effects of a mutagen and increase the number of mutagens you can store in your apparatus to 5.

Raging Resistance (9th) You resist electricity and fire damage.

Take ‘Em All On.name: Take ‘Em All On
Take ‘Em All On.description: You are not intimidated by vast hordes of opponents, delving into the depths of combat to destroy your enemies en masse. Your additional damage from Rage triggers weaknesses to area damage and you gain your raging resistance against damage dealt to you by swarms or troops or increase your raging resistance by 5 if you would already resist the damage they deal.

Instinct Crown (Bloodrager).name: Instinct Crown (Bloodrager)
Instinct Crown (Bloodrager).description:
An instinct crown is a magical headpiece imbued with the essence of instincts that barbarians draw upon in combat. Each crown is fashioned to represent the instinct it's tied to, such as a wolf's head for an animal instinct crown or a simple helmet with Jotun runes for a giant instinct crown. When worn, the crown allows you to tap further into your instincts, granting you even greater benefits if the crown's essence matches your instinct. You must be able to Rage to use the crown's activations.

Activate F envision

Frequency once per day

Trigger You roll initiative

Effect You Rage, gaining 10 additional temporary Hit Points.

Activate 2 command, envision

Requirements The crown's instinct matches your barbarian instinct

Frequency once per day

Effect Your connection to magic is pushed to its limits. You become quickened until the end of your rage. You can use your extra action for the action you gained to Harvest Blood.

Heartened.name: Heartened
Heartened.description:
Your determination empowers you to go beyond what is safe to save those you care about. You do not gain the Quick Tempered free action. You’re trained in Diplomacy instead of Athletics from the barbarian class and you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Diplomacy checks while raging. When you use the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.HCl3pzVefiv9ZKQW]{Aid} reaction, you can choose to roll [[/act aid statistic=diplomacy traits=linguistic]]{Diplomacy} instead of the normal skill check by speaking encouraging words, giving your Aid the linguistic trait.

When you succeed at a Diplomacy check that would benefit an ally in an encounter, you become invigorated until the end of your next turn. You grant the ally you affected with your Diplomacy check the temporary Hit Points of your invigoration instead of yourself that last for as long as you are invigorated. If you grant temporary Hit Points to an ally, any temporary Hit Points you granted to a previous ally are immediately lost. You gain the Bolster Hope free action.

Invigoration Bonus You grant the affected ally temporary Hit Points and you gain a +2 status bonus to saves against fear effects. If any ally in the current encounter gains the dying condition, you are no longer invigorated and you both lose these effects.

Elemental Instinct (Alternate).name: Elemental Instinct (Alternate)
Elemental Instinct (Alternate).description:
While some elementals surround those with the instinct, others find they can better focus on their inner gates of strength for ending conflicts with ease.

This instinct option for barbarians allows you to channel elemental forces, bonding with a single element and its associated plane. Perhaps your ancestors were elemental conjurers or blessed by an elemental lord. Select an element from the Elemental Instincts table to be your instinct's element. If your element offers multiple damage types, choose one of those type when you select your element.

ElementTraitDamage
AirAirElectricity or slashing
EarthEarthBludgeoning or piercing
FireFireFire
MetalMetalPiercing or slashing
WaterWaterBludgeoning or cold
WoodWoodBludgeoning or piercing

Instinct Ability—Elemental Rage While raging, you increase the additional damage from Rage from 2 to 3 and change its damage type to the one you selected for your element. You gain the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.feats-srd.CbfszeYw3cf99kdv]{Kineticist Dedication} multiclass feat as a bonus feat, even though you don't meet its level prerequisite. If you have any kineticist impulses with the same element type as the one you chose for your instinct, such as ones gained by taking the Kineticist Dedication multiclass feat, they gain the rage trait and the Sustain action gains the rage trait when it is used to Sustain these impulses.

Special You can select the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.feats-srd.6tDIVv2gafdO6GV4]{Through the Gate} kineticist archetype feat as a 2nd-level archetype feat.

Specialization Ability When you use elemental rage, you increase the damage from Rage from 3 to 7. If you have greater weapon specialization, instead increase the damage from Rage when using elemental rage from 7 to 13.

Raging Resistance You resist the damage dealt by attacks and abilities of elemental creatures of your chosen element, as well as creatures made of your element, regardless of the damage type. You also resist damage dealt by attacks, spells, and abilities with your elemental trait.

Parley with Titans.name: Parley with Titans
Parley with Titans.description:
Your presence and mannerisms remind the most terrible of beasts of their kin, opening up a dialogue with them. You may use Intimidation rather than Diplomacy to [[/act request statistic=intimidation]]{Request} or [[/act make-an-impression statistic=intimidation]]{Make an Impression} with creatures that are size Large or larger. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to this check if the creature is of a type related to your Instinct, such as a beast, a dragon or a giant.

Special If you have the fury instinct, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your check regardless of the creature type.

Revitalizing Roar.name: Revitalizing Roar
Revitalizing Roar.description:
Trigger Your turn begins.

Requirements You are below half your total Hit Points.

With a terrible howl, you vent out your pain, frustration and anger in the middle of a fight to give you the strength to keep fighting. You restore four times your character level in Hit Points plus your Constitution modifier (@Damage[(@actor.level * 4 + @actor.system.abilities.con.mod)[healing]]). After you use this action, your Rage immediately ends and you are @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.HL2l2VRSaQHu9lUw]{Fatigued} until you rest for at least 10 minutes.

Breach Instinct.name: Breach Instinct
Breach Instinct.description:
You stand on the veil of this world and that of another. By precariously riding the lines of the transitive planes you have become a breach between worlds yourself. Your struggle to contain your powers and the chaos of a breach is apparent in your fury, as with a single swing you can cause rifts in existence.

Instinct Ability—Breaching Blows Your attacks conjure images from your breach plane, leaving lingering figments and obstructions in their wake. Choose one of the transitive planes below. Once this choice is made it cannot be changed. Increase your damage from Rage from 2 to 4 against creatures in difficult terrain you created. You gain the Breach Blow activity.

Plane

Traits

Astral

fire, arcane

Ethereal

divine, spirit

Netherworld

darkness, occult

First World

light, primal

Specialization Ability (7th) Increase the damage from Rage from 4 to 8 against creatures in difficult terrain you created and the cone from your Breach Blow can be up to a 15-foot cone. If you have greater weapon specialization, instead increase the damage from Rage to 16 against creatures in difficult terrain you created and the cone of your Breach Blow can be up to a 20-foot cone.

Raging Resistance (9th) You resist mental damage and damage from effects with your chosen plane’s traits.

Unleash Inner Beast.name: Unleash Inner Beast
Unleash Inner Beast.description: While you rage, you can shoot manifestations of the beast inside you to savage your opponents. You gain an inner beast ranged unarmed attack that deals 1d4 force damage with a range increment of 20 feet. This unarmed attack has the force, magical, propulsive, and unarmed traits.

Giant Instinct (Alternate).name: Giant Instinct (Alternate)
Giant Instinct (Alternate).description:
While some barbarians’ rage is inspired by the concept of giants, certain among them are truly steeped in the cultures of giantdom. Some live among marauding frost giants while others may eke out a living slaying lumbering hill giants… and some are even directly descended from a particular giant clan. No matter the source, these giant barbarians call upon specific sorts of giants to empower them during combat. Select a giant type from the table below and you become trained in Giant Lore.

Instinct Ability—Titanic Weapon You are well trained in the iconic weapons of your giants' culture, able to wield them as well as the titans who have spent generations training with them. You gain a special weapon empowered by the might of giants from the above table. Your weapon might be immensely over-sized, soaked in the blood of giants or crafted alongside them in their sanctuaries. While wielding the listed weapon, the damage of your weapon is increased by one die size or by two die sizes if the weapon is an unarmed attack or a simple weapon (for example, longspear from a d8 to d12), and your additional damage from Rage increases from 2 to 3. If your weapon would increase its die size above a d12, such as a greataxe, your additional damage from Rage increases from 2 to 4 and your weapon gains the razing trait while you’re raging.

* Your blunderbuss gains the kickback trait and deals your Rage damage while within its first range increment. If you would increase your reach (such as from Giant Stature), you also increase the range increment your blunderbuss by the same amount.

** Your composite longbow deals your full Strength damage and half your Rage damage while within its first range increment. If you would increase your reach (such as from Giant Stature), you also increase the range increment of your composite longbow by the same amount.

Blood Surge Devastation.name: Blood Surge Devastation
Blood Surge Devastation.description:
Trigger You critically succeed at a Strike that would deal additional damage from rage.

Channeling your fury to untold heights, you cause huge lashes of power to rip through your surroundings. You cast @UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-barbarians.items.hiqoZc3SW8BAuTOO]{Blood Surge}.

Embrace the Eldritch.name: Embrace the Eldritch
Embrace the Eldritch.description:
Trigger You are the target of a spell or magical effect that requires a save.

Requirements You’re not frightened.

You know that magic is dangerous, but to face the eldritch with the heart of a warrior is to make it powerless, for fear is but a welcome partner in the war against the unnartural. You treat your degree of success on the triggering save as one step better. This counts as willingly accepting the effects of a spell for the purposes of your instinct and you become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Greater Harness Bloodline.name: Greater Harness Bloodline
Greater Harness Bloodline.description: You complete your final step into the blood. You gain your bloodline’s greater bloodline spell.

Become Ancestor.name: Become Ancestor
Become Ancestor.description: When you wield your vestige weapon, you and your ancestor merge into one being, your personality changing and your appearance becoming that of the ancestor. Choose two attribute modifiers when you first gain this feat, one must be Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution, and the other must be Charisma, Intelligence, or Wisdom. While raging, you either increase the chosen attribute modifier by 1 or increase it to +4, whichever would give you a higher value. Your vestige weapon gains the apex trait while you are raging and you cannot benefit from any other apex items while you are benefiting from your vestige weapon.

Hurling Might.name: Hurling Might
Hurling Might.description: In a fit of anger, you can throw weapons as hard as you can at enemies out of your reach. All melee weapons you wield gain the thrown 10 feet trait while you are raging or increase their thrown range by 10 feet if the weapon already had the thrown trait. You do not take a penalty to attack rolls for using improvised weapons when they are thrown.

Rage Tattoos.name: Rage Tattoos
Rage Tattoos.description: You can craft tattoos, including magical tattoos. You gain the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.feats-srd.BocFD2KV0qgUC76x]{Additional Lore} general feat for Tattoo Lore and can @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.rmwa3OyhTZ2i2AHl]{Craft} tattoos using Tattoo Lore instead of Crafting. When you select this feat, you gain the formulas for four common magical tattoos of 2nd level or lower. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Tattoo Lore checks to Craft tattoos on yourself. If you're a master in Tattoo Lore, this bonus increases to +2 and you gain the formulas for four common magical tattoos of 7th level or lower.

Vestige Instinct.name: Vestige Instinct
Vestige Instinct.description:
You are descended from a legendary hero like First Emperor Taldaris, Khan Budugan of Hongal, or Saebjorn Arm-Fang. When you dive into battle, you can feel the remnants of their legend burning inside you.

Instinct Ability—Inherited Rage In battle, you channel the wrath of your legacy. Your ancestor is bonded to you through a weapon, and you start with this weapon for free. When you rage, your weapon empowers you and you take on aspects of your ancestors' physical form and your rage gains the polymorph and occult traits. If your vestige weapon is a simple weapon, increase the damage die size of that weapon by one step. Your vestige weapon also gains either the deadly d6 or razing trait. If the weapon has one of these traits, you must select the other trait. While wielding your vestige weapon, you increase the additional damage from Rage from 2 to 3.

Specialization Ability (7th) Increase the additional damage from Rage from 3 to 7. If you have greater weapon specialization, instead increase the additional damage from Rage to 13.

Raging Resistance (9th) You resist mental damage and spirit damage.

Forestbutcher.name: Forestbutcher
Forestbutcher.description: Designed by countercultural elves who admired the aesthetic of Treerazer, wielder of the Blackaxe (and thus found incredibly distasteful by most elves), forestbutcher axes cleave trees and men alike. Their blades are weighted and designed in such a way to cut into the grooves of wood and easily separate them. Forestbutchers deal 1 additional precision damage per weapon damage die to creatures with the plant or wood traits.

Spellbreaking Charge.name: Spellbreaking Charge
Spellbreaking Charge.description: You rampage through the field with a charge so powerful it can shatter magic itself. Stride and then either attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.SjmKHgI7a5Z9JzBx]{Force Open} a barrier or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.7blmbDrQFNfdT731]{Shove} a creature and then attempt to counteract a magical effect affecting the target, using your spell DC - 10 as the counteract modifier for the check and the highest rank spell you can cast as the counter rank. If the target was a barrier spell and you succeed at your counteract, the spell immediately ends. Targets still take the normal effects of your action regardless of whether or not you succeed in counteracting the effect.

Bark Barricade.name: Bark Barricade
Bark Barricade.description: Your forearms have developed into thick logs, allowing you to fend off even the greatest attack. You gain the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.classfeatures.eZNCckLzbH3GyncH]{Shield Block} feat. Once per 10 minutes, you can spend a single action with the manipulate trait to create a wooden shield in one of your hands that lasts for 1 minute and you can @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.xjGwis0uaC2305pm]{Raise a Shield} as part of your action to create it. The shield is destroyed immediately if you stop holding it, withering into dead branches. Wooden shields you create are 1 Bulk and have an AC bonus of +2, a Hardness equal to your level + 3, and Hit Points equal to twice your level with a Broken Threshold equal to your level.

Gigauntlets.name: Gigauntlets
Gigauntlets.description: These enormous gauntlets serve as bulky replacements to the normal gauntlets from most heavy armors. You cannot wield weapons when armed with gigauntlets even though they have the free-hand trait and you cannot perform actions that would require you to use a set of tools to perform (such as @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.s1vB3HdXjMigYAnY]{healer’s toolkit}).

Essence Sap.name: Essence Sap
Essence Sap.description: As the faculties of others are depleted, your aberrative manifestations feast. Choose a creature adjacent to you with one of the following conditions: clumsy, dazzled, deafened, enfeebled, fascinated, frightened, paralyzed, stunned, or stupefied. The creature takes damage equal to your additional damage from rage and you regain a number of hit points equal to the damage dealt (@Check[type:will|basic:true|against:classDC] save against your class DC).

Instinct Crown (Untamed).name: Instinct Crown (Untamed)
Instinct Crown (Untamed).description:
An instinct crown is a magical headpiece imbued with the essence of instincts that barbarians draw upon in combat. Each crown is fashioned to represent the instinct it's tied to, such as a wolf's head for an animal instinct crown or a simple helmet with Jotun runes for a giant instinct crown. When worn, the crown allows you to tap further into your instincts, granting you even greater benefits if the crown's essence matches your instinct. You must be able to Rage to use the crown's activations.

Activate F envision

Frequency once per day

Trigger You roll initiative

Effect You Rage, gaining 10 additional temporary Hit Points.

Activate 2 command, envision

Requirements The crown's instinct matches your barbarian instinct

Frequency once per day

Effect You and your companion have learned to tear the flesh of your enemies in unison. Your animal companion uses Rage and becomes quickened until the end of its rage. It can use its extra action to Support or Strike. If you and your animal companion successfully Strike the same target during your turn, your animal companion can spend a single action to Rend the target using the damage of the unarmed attack that your animal companion used for the Strike.

Rune Swap.name: Rune Swap
Rune Swap.description: Your runes can be morphed into other runes through magical concentration. You can spend 10 minutes to change one of the runes you selected for Runic Marks to another rune of your choice, replacing the effects of the rune with the newly selected rune. This change is permanent until you choose to change your runes again.

Chaos of the Wildblooded.name: Chaos of the Wildblooded
Chaos of the Wildblooded.description: Even in your calmest moments, you are never more than an instant away from channeling mass destruction through your magic. Whenever you take damage from a spell, you are @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.nlCjDvLMf2EkV2dl]{Quickened} until the end of your next turn. You can use your extra action to Strike or to cast @UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-barbarians.items.hiqoZc3SW8BAuTOO]{Blood Surge}.

Volatile Rage.name: Volatile Rage
Volatile Rage.description: The chemicals you imbibe are not safe for consumption, and yet when you rage, they empower you nonetheless. You learn the formula for 6 alchemical bombs. When you store versatile vials in your apparatus, you can use @UUID[Compendium.pf2e-team-plus-barbarians.misc.i0Urwze7pbBPVx3X]{Mad Science} to create a bomb and then consume it instead of a mutagen. Consuming a bomb in this way counts as consuming a mutagen for mutagenic rage. When you consume a bomb, your additional damage from Rage changes its damage type to match that of your bomb instead of the damage type for your weapon or unarmed attack.

Axewheel.name: Axewheel
Axewheel.description: This circular frame with mounted axe blades serves as a means for a deadly weapon in both close range combat, and against enemies within range of a deadly throw.

Extraneous Limbs.name: Extraneous Limbs
Extraneous Limbs.description: You gain additional limbs that you can use when you are raging. You gain 2 additional appendages, which allow you to hold up to four hands’ worth of weapons and equipment. You must designate a pair of appendages as your active hands and you choose which pair is active when you use this ability. You can only wield items in your active hands, but you can take simple Interact actions with your other limbs. You can change this designation from one pair of hands to another by taking this action again.

Know the Breach.name: Know the Breach
Know the Breach.description: You have learned to understand the planes through your constant connection to them. You gain the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.feats-srd.BocFD2KV0qgUC76x]{Additional Lore} general feat for your chosen plane and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} checks for this Lore gain the rage trait while you are raging. You gain a +1 status bonus to saves against effects produced by creatures that originate from your chosen plane.

Mountain Hammer.name: Mountain Hammer
Mountain Hammer.description: This hammer’s head is a slab of stone as large as a dwarf, held together by iron bands. Its sheer weight means it is often dragged around, then brought in a terrible arc directly into an enemy’s skull.
